study_type_evidence.quote: Frozen plasma matrices were thawed and centrifuged at 3100 rpm (2074x g) for 5 to 10 min at 4 degrees C.
The binding of HM-10/10 to proteins in CD-1 mouse, Sprague-Dawley rat, beagle dog, cynomolgus monkey, and human plasma was successfully determined
The stability of HM-10/10 was tested in simulated gastric fluid (SGF) and simulated intestinal fluid (SIF) over 120 min.
In the metabolizing enzyme-specific environment of human liver microsomes, HM-10/10 demonstrated good stability.
The half-life and intrinsic clearance values of HM-10/10 were investigated in hepatocytes of the same array of animal models

ex_vivo_detail: Plasma drug-stability and plasma protein-binding assays were run in previously frozen K2EDTA plasma from CD-1 mouse, Sprague-Dawley rat, beagle dog, cynomolgus monkey and human. Per protocol these plasma-matrix assays are classified ex vivo (animal = mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey; human = human plasma).
in_vitro_detail: Cell-free / subcellular / buffer systems: pooled liver microsomes (CD-1 mouse, Sprague-Dawley rat, beagle dog, cynomolgus monkey, human) at 0.5 mg protein/mL with NADPH; cryopreserved hepatocytes (same five species) at 0.5 million cells/mL; simulated gastric fluid (pH 1.3) and simulated intestinal fluid (pH 5.5); 0.1 M potassium phosphate buffers at pH 1.3, 5.5 and 7.4; CYP450 time-dependent inhibition in pooled human liver microsomes; CYP450 induction in three single-donor lots of pre-plated human hepatocytes (HH1086, HH1142, HH1144).

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Stability of HM-10/10 in plasma matrices determined by compound concentration measurements over a 120 min time course via triple quadrupole mass spectrometer.
concentration_time_figure.note: Percent-remaining / concentration versus time plots rather than in vivo plasma concentration-time curves. Figure 1 = plasma matrices (includes CD-1 mouse) over 120 min; Figure 2 = simulated gastric and intestinal fluid over 120 min; Figure 3 = pH 1.3, 5.5 and 7.4 buffers over 120 min; Figure 4 = liver microsomes over 120 min. No animal was dosed, so no true in vivo PK profile exists.

bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS: Waters XSELECT HSS T3 2.5 µm 30 x 2.1 mm column with formic acid water/acetonitrile gradient, detected on an Applied Biosystems Sciex API-5500 triple quadrupole mass spectrometer with positive-ion electrospray ionization, multiple-reaction-monitoring; RT-PCR/SYBR Green used for CYP450 mRNA induction endpoints
bioanalytical_quote: Analytes and internal standards were detected using an Applied Biosystems Sciex API-5500 triple quadrupole mass spectrometer with Agilent 1260 Infinity Binary Pump
notes: Pure ADME stability-characterization study; no animal or human was dosed, so there are no in vivo PK parameters (no Cmax, Tmax, AUC, dose or route). Only half-lives from incubations are available. Full set of HM-10/10 half-lives reported in the body: plasma (Table 1) human 164 min, Sprague-Dawley rat 82.5 min, beagle dog 54.6 min, cynomolgus monkey 52.7 min, CD-1 mouse 5.68 min; simulated gastric fluid 372 min and simulated intestinal fluid 2.72 min (Table 2); buffer pH 1.3 and 5.5 could not be determined (>120 min), pH 7.4 = 433 min (Table 3); liver microsomes (Table 4) CD-1 mouse 32.0 min, rat 27.7 min, dog 33.0 min, monkey 21.8 min, human 20.3 min; hepatocytes (Table 5) CD-1 mouse <15 min, rat 5.81 min, dog 10.7 min, monkey 12.1 min, human 5.28 min. Note the PEPLIFE2 header row lists 32.5 min for CD-1 mouse liver microsomes whereas Table 4 in the body states 32.0 min; the body value was used. Plasma protein binding in CD-1 mouse was 15.3 +/- 24.6% bound (Table 6). CYP450 positive-control inhibitors and inducers are listed as reference-standard agents; substrate probes (phenacetin, bupropion, amodiaquine, diclofenac, mephenytoin, dextromethorphan, midazolam, testosterone) and internal standards (carbutamide, chrysin, glyburide, Feng#1 SIL) were also used but are analytical reagents rather than tested articles. Body reports no ex vivo/in vitro half-life for warfarin or for the CYP control compounds.
